rejected.title: Vertices, edges and degree
card: Vertex
a point on a graph, often drawn as a dot. It can stand for a place, a person or a team.
Edge
a line that joins two vertices. It can stand for a road, a friendship or a match between two teams.
Degree
the number of edges that meet a vertex. A vertex with 3 edges meeting it has degree 3.
Example: a graph has vertices A, B, C and D, with edges AB, AC, AD and BC. A has 3 edges meeting it, so its degree is 3. D has only AD, so its degree is 1.
rejected.remember: Count the edges at a vertex to find its degree, not the vertices it touches by name.

a.q: A graph has vertices P, Q, R and S, and edges PQ, PR, PS and QR. What is the degree of vertex R?
a.why: The edges meeting R are PR and QR, so the degree of R is 2. The answer 3 is the degree of P, which has PQ, PR and PS.
a.clue: List only the edges that include the letter R.

b.q: A graph shows five towns as vertices and has 6 edges for the roads between them. The towns have degrees 3, 3, 2, 2 and 2. Which town has the most roads meeting it?
b.why: Degree is the number of edges meeting a vertex, so the largest degree has the most roads. The largest degree listed is 3. The number 6 counts all the edges on the graph, not the edges at one town.
b.clue: Which degree in the list is the largest?

version.title: Vertices, edges and degree
card: Vertex
a point on a graph, drawn as a dot. It can stand for a place, a person or a team.
Edge
a line joining two vertices. It can stand for a road, a friendship or a game between two teams.
Degree
the number of edges that meet a vertex. With edges AB, AC, AD and BC, vertex A has degree 3 and D has degree 1.
Each edge adds 1 to the degree at each of its two ends. So the degrees of all the vertices add up to twice the number of edges.
version.remember: Degree counts the edges at one vertex. All the degrees together make twice the number of edges.

a.q: A graph has vertices P, Q, R, S and T, with edges PQ, QR, QS, RS and ST. What is the degree of vertex S?
a.why: The edges that meet S are QS, RS and ST, so its degree is 3. The answer 5 is the number of edges in the whole graph, not the edges at S.
a.clue: List only the edges that include the letter S.

b.q: A network of 6 towns has roads joining them. The towns have degrees 4, 3, 3, 2, 2 and 2. How many roads are in the network?
b.why: The degrees add to 4 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 16. Each road adds 1 to the degree at both of its ends, so it is counted twice: 16 ÷ 2 = 8 roads. The answer 16 forgets to halve.
b.clue: Each road is counted once at each end.
